evidence: Compared leftOutReason (engine/review/app/findings.go:93-113) with severeFinding (engine/reviewverdict/decide.go:98-122) for every combination of causal disposition, head result, base_result and no verdict. They agree.
pre-existing and base-only are left out before any verdict is read. This matches fateOfTheBase.
For unknown disposition, head not-reproduced returns ReasonNotReproduced first. This matches fateRefuted, and the base check does not run ahead of it.
For unknown disposition with base reproduced and head reproduced or not-run, the finding is left out as base-reproduced. This matches fateOfTheBase.
For unknown disposition with base not-reproduced or not-run, the finding is kept. This matches fateBlocks or fateUnchecked.
For introduced, behavior-activated and worsened dispositions, base_result is ignored. This matches severeFinding.
With no verdict, the finding is kept. Decide reads it as an unchecked finding, so it is listed as unverified.

The four help texts (engine/cmd/usage.go:268-269, bin/lib/usage.sh:396-402, README.md:829-833, odd/review-results/README.md:47) state the same rule and the same reason string, `verdict base-reproduced`.

TestFindingsKeepsASevereFindingExactlyWhenDecideListsItAsBlockingOrUnverified (engine/review/app/findings_test.go:239-272) runs BLOCKER and CRITICAL over 6 dispositions, 3 head results plus no verdict, and 3 base results. It compares each against reviewverdict.Decide, so a drift in either function fails it.

TestFindingsLeavesOutASevereUnknownFindingTheVerdictFoundOnBase and TestFindingsKeepsWhatTheBaseRuleDoesNotReach (findings_test.go:202-235) pin the reason string and the boundary cases. These include base reproduced with head not-reproduced, which keeps not-reproduced as the reason.
The wrapper parity test and the README test (engine/cmd/review_test.go:1242-1292) assert the new reason phrase in the engine usage, the wrapper usage and the README.
